name: Cystic Hygroma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Cystic Hygroma

criteria.description: Presence of a soft, compressible, multiloculated cystic mass typically located in the cervicofacial region
Ultrasound showing multiloculated cystic lesions with thin septations and absence of internal vascular flow
MRI demonstrating fluid-filled cystic spaces with characteristic signal intensities consistent with lymphatic malformation
Histopathological confirmation showing dilated lymphatic channels lined by endothelial cells

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical presentation of characteristic cystic mass plus confirmatory imaging findings (ultrasound or MRI)
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Prenatal diagnosis is possible via ultrasound; histopathology is confirmatory but not always required.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiloculated cystic mass in cervicofacial region
searchTerms: multi-chambered cystic mass in neck or face

pathognomonic.notes: Usually present at birth or early infancy

common.notes: Due to mass effect in large lesions
searchTerms: difficulty breathing due to airway blockage

common.symptomName: Cosmetic deformity of the neck or face
searchTerms: visible deformity of neck or face
light passes through cyst on exam

occasional.notes: May cause erythema, tenderness, and fever
Can cause sudden swelling and pain

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to mass effect
searchTerms: neurological issues due to tumor size
swelling due to lymph fluid buildup

rare.notes: May be detected prenatally or postnatally

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests unless infected or hemorrhagic
imaging: Ultrasound showing multiloculated cystic mass with thin septations
MRI demonstrating fluid-filled lymphatic spaces without solid components
Prenatal ultrasound detection of cystic mass
genetic: Possible association with Noonan syndrome and other chromosomal anomalies
other: Histopathology showing dilated lymphatic channels lined by endothelial cells

distinguishingFeatures: Located along anterior border of sternocleidomastoid
No multiloculated cystic spaces on imaging
Solid vascular mass with blood flow on Doppler ultrasound
Rapid postnatal growth followed by involution
Moves with swallowing or tongue protrusion

redFlags: Signs of infection such as fever, erythema, and tenderness
Neurological deficits indicating mass effect on cranial nerves
references: Wassef M, Blei F, Adams D, et al. Vascular Anomalies Classification: Recommendations From the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies. Pediatrics. 2015;136(1):e203-e214.
Mulliken JB, Glowacki J. Hemangiomas and vascular malformations in infants and children: a classification based on endothelial characteristics. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1982 Mar;69(3):412-22.
